If it does, the subquery no longer correlates with the fund and EXISTS / NOT EXISTS gives the same result for every fund. The intended reading (gen_fundmain.gen_customeridnumber = Gen_companyworker.Gen_identitynumber) is a hypothesis.

Set at runtime from CRM table gen_etlvariable (gen_key = variable name, gen_scope global or package name). The actual domain names, and therefore which SystemUser becomes owner, are data, not in the DTSX. Design-time defaults FormDB / FromDB (DTSX:28, 46) are overwritten, or the Set Variables script throws if the key is missing.
Package loads XML configuration C:\Generix\SSISConfigFile.dtsConfig (DTSX:16-18), not supplied (external_unknown); it may override the [CRM] connection or variables.

notes.note: Business CRM writers: 8 OLE DB Commands, all direct SQL UPDATE on CRM Base tables over [CRM] (Unsupported), 3 attributes each (ownerid, owningbusinessunit, owneridtype) = 24 attribute mappings, plus the record key. None is byte-identical (dupes.json is empty): CW vs Regular flows differ in EXISTS vs NOT EXISTS, in the variable used (CompanyEmployeesDomainName vs RegularFundsDomainName) and in the target table; the Trans/MF flows differ in the child table. The lineage script writer End ETL Process record\ETL Record Finish and the Create/Error ETL Process record script tasks are ETL plumbing (not mapped). No flat files in this package.

Execution order (Success constraints DTSX:5115-5124): Get Variables -> Create ETL Process record -> Update CW Funds -> Update Regular Funds -> Update Trans -> Update MF Current Year -> Update MF Previous Year -> Update MF Archive -> Update CW FTRequests -> Update Regular FTRequest -> End ETL Process record.

Business meaning (from the SQL, not from names): funds (gen_fundmain) and FT requests (gen_ftrequest) whose customer id number matches a Gen_companyworker identity number are reassigned to the system user whose domainname = @[User::CompanyEmployeesDomainName]; all other funds / FT requests not already owned by a user with that DomainName are reassigned to the user with domainname = @[User::RegularFundsDomainName]. Then gen_ftcurrentyear, gen_mfcurrentyear, gen_mfpreviousyear and gen_mfarchive records inherit OwnerId / OwningBusinessUnit / OwnerIdType from their gen_fundmain (via gen_fundnumber) when different.

Owner changes are done by direct SQL on Base tables: CRM ownership side effects (sharing / PrincipalObjectAccess, cascade assign of related records, audit, plugins / workflows, modifiedon / modifiedby) are bypassed; the package itself propagates owners only to the four child tables listed.

Positional binding (all 8 commands): SQL 'set [OwnerId]=?, [OwningBusinessUnit]=?, [OwnerIdType]=? where [<id>] = ?' -> Param_0 = OwnerId, Param_1 = OwningBusinessUnit, Param_2 = OwnerIdType, Param_3 = record id (component.mjs input -> ext:Param_k matches the order of the '?').

'Get MF' x3 and 'Get ft' carry ParameterMapping '"Parameter0:Input",{8C07AFF0-B44D-4A94-BBCF-C5ECCAC23605}' (DTSX:3803, 3990, 4177, 4949) although their SQL has no '?'; no variable with that DTSID exists in the package (variables: CompanyEmployeesDomainName {96B6AFE4...}, RegularFundsDomainName {781FC0E7...}, ...). Stale mapping; no effect on the written values is provable either way.
Lookups get user / Get User use Partial cache on SystemUser.domainname; if several SystemUser rows share the domain name, which row is returned is not defined.
The CW / Regular sources exclude records owned by teams (inner join SystemUser on systemuserid = OwnerId) and records whose owner's DomainName is NULL (NULL != ? is not true).
OLE DB source output columns appear in lineage openItems (output null, async) because the graph ends at the SQL expression; they are DB origins, not unresolved script hops.
